pages.text: Milo lived in a tall white lighthouse by the sea. Every evening, his grandpa climbed the long stairs and lit the great lamp at the top.
“The light keeps the boats safe,” Grandpa always said. “When the sea is dark, our lamp shows them the way home.” Milo loved to watch it shine.
One autumn night, a storm came. The wind howled, and the rain beat against the windows. Far out at sea, Old Otter's little red boat was sailing home.
Suddenly, everything went dark. The great lamp had gone out! Grandpa turned the switch again and again, but nothing happened. The lighthouse stood blind in the storm.
“The storm broke the lamp,” said Grandpa. “I must fix it, but it will take time.” His voice was worried. “And Old Otter is still out at sea.”
Milo looked out into the black night. Without the light, Old Otter could not find the harbor. The waves were tall and strong. Milo had to do something.
Then he remembered the meadow behind the lighthouse. On summer nights, it was full of fireflies! “Maybe they can help us,” Milo said, and he ran down the stairs.
The fireflies were hiding from the rain under the leaves. “Please,” said Milo, “a boat is lost in the dark. Will you shine with me?” The fireflies blinked kindly.
Hundreds of fireflies followed Milo up the long, long stairs. Together they made a big, warm ball of golden light at the top of the lighthouse.
Out at sea, Old Otter saw a soft golden glow. “There!” he cried. “There is the lighthouse!” He turned his little red boat toward the light.
The boat sailed slowly through the tall waves, closer and closer. At last, it slipped safely into the harbor. Old Otter was home.
Just then, Grandpa fixed the great lamp. It flashed on, bright and strong. The fireflies cheered — well, they blinked very fast, which is how fireflies cheer.
“You saved the night, Milo,” said Grandpa proudly. “A small light is still a light. And many small lights together can be as bright as the sun.”
The next morning, Old Otter brought them a basket of fresh fish. And every summer after that, the fireflies came to visit the little mouse who had asked them for help.
